summary: ING's current-account pages sit in the traditional camp but lean towards the challengers: the offer is clearly stated, the layout is mobile-first and the desire score is maximal, so the core proposition is not the problem. What separates ING from the peer set is intensity — roughly four urgency markers per page against a peer mean of 0.64, five persuasion techniques against 1.67, and pages almost twice as long as peers, on a much brighter background. None of this is linked to any click, conversion or sale in the data, so every point below is a hypothesis to test, not a proven cause.

recommendations.title: Cut urgency and deadline language down to near zero
recommendations.finding: Urgency and deadline language is ING's single largest deviation from the market: 4.0 markers per page against a peer mean of 0.64, a gap of 3.69 standard deviations, and 2.5 standard deviations from the market overall. This is an automatic, countable measure rather than a judgement call, so the size of the gap is solid even though its effect on behaviour is unmeasured.
recommendations.recommendation: Audit every deadline, countdown and 'only until' phrasing on the current-account pages and keep at most one genuine, dated deadline per page. Where a deadline is not a real regulatory or product cut-off, replace it with a plain statement of the offer.

recommendations.title: Thin out the stacked persuasion techniques
recommendations.finding: ING uses 5.0 persuasion techniques per page where peers average 1.67, a gap of 3.68 standard deviations and a 2.5 standard deviation signature against the market. The count is rubric-scored by a single judge, so treat the size of the gap as indicative rather than exact, but the direction is consistent with the urgency finding.
recommendations.recommendation: Per page, pick one primary persuasive argument for the account pack and remove the secondary levers that repeat it — instead of stacking scarcity, social proof and reassurance in the same block, sequence them across the page or drop the weaker ones.

recommendations.title: Make the 'free account' claim carry its conditions visibly
recommendations.finding: On 0.67 of ING pages the free claim carries conditions attached, against a peer mean of 0.23 — a gap of 1.03 standard deviations. ING also already runs legal small print on 93% of traditional-bank pages versus 50% at challengers, so the conditions exist; the issue is how prominently they sit relative to the free headline.
recommendations.recommendation: Place the qualifying condition (minimum deposit, salary transfer, age or package requirement) in the same visual block as the word 'free', at readable size, rather than only in the footer small print. Keep the legal disclaimer, but stop relying on it as the only disclosure.

recommendations.title: Shorten the current-account pages and lift the offer above the fold
recommendations.finding: ING pages run to 11148.67 pixels against a peer mean of 6411.72, a gap of 1.42 standard deviations. The offer itself is not the weak point — clarity of the offer scores 5.0 against 3.97 — so length is adding volume rather than adding information.
recommendations.recommendation: Set a target page length close to the peer mean and cut the repeating blocks first: duplicated product explanations, restated conditions and secondary cross-sell panels. Keep the clearest offer statement in the opening screen and move supporting detail into expandable sections.

recommendations.title: Substantiate the fast digital sign-up promise
recommendations.finding: Promises of fast digital sign-up appear on 0.67 of ING pages against a peer mean of 0.15, but this is a model-assisted measure produced by more than one model, so part of the gap may be measurement rather than copy. The evidence is thin: the promise is frequent, its effect on sign-up completion is unknown, and no performance data exists in this study.
recommendations.recommendation: Keep the digital sign-up promise but attach a concrete, checkable proof point next to it — the number of steps, the documents needed, or the moment the account becomes usable — so the claim can be verified by the reader instead of asserted.

recommendations.title: Consolidate many small images into fewer, larger visuals
recommendations.finding: ING carries 33 images per page against a peer mean of 19, yet the share of the page that is imagery sits at 0.10 for traditional banks versus 0.31 for challengers, and the opening image at 0.25 versus 0.62. ING therefore has many images but a comparatively small visual footprint — the opposite of the challenger pattern.
recommendations.recommendation: Replace clusters of small decorative images with one dominant hero visual per page and let the remaining imagery support specific sections. Note that the opening-image measure is affected by cookie-consent overlays at three other banks, so compare ING's own pages before and after rather than relying on the cross-bank gap alone.

recommendations.title: Review the very bright page surfaces
recommendations.finding: Page brightness measures 0.55 at ING against a peer mean of 0.34, and brightness is one of the strongest separators in the dataset: traditional banks average 0.43 and challengers 0.17. Read this as a comparison of our captures only — it is measured on a single rendering in a default light colour scheme, and dark-mode visitors may see something different.
recommendations.recommendation: Test a calmer surface treatment behind the hero and offer blocks — a lower-luminance background or a contained coloured section rather than an all-over bright field — and check it in both light and dark rendering before rolling it out.

recommendations.title: Protect the mobile-first layout and the desire score while trimming
recommendations.finding: Two of ING's measured strengths are already at the ceiling: designed mobile-first scores 1.0 against a peer mean of 0.56, and makes the offer feel worth having scores 1.0 against 0.59. Clarity of the offer (5.0 vs 3.97) is also above peers. These are the assets to preserve while cutting urgency, persuasion stacking and length.
recommendations.recommendation: Treat mobile-first layout and the desirability of the offer as guardrails in the redesign: when removing blocks, remove them from the desktop presentation first and verify on mobile that the value proposition and the primary call to action are still the first things seen.

recommendations.title: Do not build the page around a digital-leadership claim the news does not echo
recommendations.finding: Across the last 90 days ING has 2 headlines in this dataset and both fall under the theme 'other'; there is no innovation_digital coverage recorded for ING at all, while BNP Paribas Fortis has 1 innovation_digital headline and Revolut 1. If ING's pages lead with a digital-leadership framing, that framing is not being reinforced by what is being written about the bank right now. This is a hypothesis to verify, not evidence about page performance, and theme counts say nothing about how any page performed.
recommendations.recommendation: Keep digital sign-up as a functional, proof-backed message rather than a leadership claim, and test a version of the current-account page whose headline leads with the concrete account proposition instead of a broader digital positioning.
recommendations.reputation_context: ING's 90-day themes are 'other' with 2 headlines and no innovation_digital theme; the two notable headlines given are an analyst-favourites item and a piece on daily transfer limits across banks.

recommendations.title: Keep fee and transfer-limit disclosure factual, and separate it from urgency framing
recommendations.finding: One of only two ING headlines in the window sits in a cross-bank story about daily transfer limits, and the other is an analyst note; both are recorded under the theme 'other'. Practical payment conditions are therefore part of the current news context around the bank. Pairing limit and fee information with deadline or scarcity language risks amplifying an operational topic with unrelated framing. The link is a hypothesis to verify; theme counts are topics, not sentiment and not performance.
recommendations.recommendation: Place transfer limits, fees and eligibility in a plain, clearly labelled disclosure block on the current-account and open-account pages, position it close to the relevant product claim, and deliberately keep it free of countdowns, 'last chance' phrasing or promotional styling.
recommendations.reputation_context: ING has 2 headlines in the 90-day window, both under the theme 'other', one of which is a cross-bank article on daily transfer limits ('Vos virements limités à 5.000 € par jour').
